pr_body:
Previously, the contents of this slice were almost not validated. This has become a problem because the declarative schema changer relies on it to forbid schema changes concurrent with the legacy schema changer. This patch addresses this by adding the missing validation logic. Henceforth a nonempty MutationJobs slice implies a nonempty Mutations slice.

Fixes #87945.

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/91747)

Thanks for the review!

bors r+

Jira issue: CRDB-19608
comments: This one is alarming to me. The good news is that the error will surface to the user immediately, so hopefully we'll get a support ticket or some user telling us what happened.

This will happen if you have a mutation job but no mutations, we won't trigger the problems in the builder but we will run into this failure:
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/e3124b11a36c730ae10f1b2d2d94d7f0d7f57123/pkg/sql/catalog/descriptor.go#L222-L224

Here we check on both the mutations and the mutation jobs 
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2675c7c0481bb33eb9f43f1c2b52c152fca3ae2d/pkg/sql/catalog/tabledesc/table_desc.go#L66-L68

In validation, we check for just one side of this condition.

Instead we ought to detect the corrupt state and return a user visible error from the builder.
This seems like it's a one-liner fix, let's do it.

review_comments: nit: Can we add a comment here that says something like "validate one mutation ID corresponds to exactly one mutation job"?

Just curious: Why is this implementation for table descriptor slightly different than any other descriptors (database, schema, type descriptor, etc.)? In all the other places, we only check the first half (i.e. for all other descriptors, it's just `return desc.declarativeSchemachangeState != nil && ...job != invalidJobID`)?

In other words, in what case will we see a nil `DeclarativeSchemaChangerState` but non empty `desc.MutationJobs`? If that happens, how can we conclude that the existence of mutation jobs are from concurrent declarative schema changers? It seems possible to get a mutation job from somewhere else, in which this function should return "false", right?

I actually forgot about types, but other descriptor kinds don't have mutations, so that's why tables (and types!) are special.

FYI there is no such thing as a "mutation job", just legacy schema changer jobs associated with mutations.
